strings.SKN_Patchwork_Colony_desc:
A disjointed product created from colonial mismanagement, the Leeward Islands is an administrative union composed of the many sparsely populated islands dotted across the northeastern stretches of the Caribbean.

Like a Frankenstein's monster of disparate states, the local governments of the islands are constantly resentful of one another. As Nevis and Anguilla remain defiant of St. John's political dominance, the continuous tension between the administrations has rendered an anti-colonial united front eternally an ideal, never manifesting into reality.
strings.SKN_Underdevelopment_desc:
While a plantation economy that ran on low-wage labor was a sustainable practice during the colonial regime, such a rudimentary system based solely on sugar export had not produced a healthy trade balance for the unfortunate Leewards. Whereas the fall of Britain and France had already cut off the sole source of foreign income of the islands, Canada's failure to redevelop viable replacement sectors had further damaged the prospects for the populace to escape severe poverty.

The masses are resentful of the Anglo elites, both for their unwarranted arrogance and their litany of mismanagement. Now, with little outside backing, the isolated gentry have outright turned into an ostracized minority, spurned by everyone save their own. As the whites wealthy enough to quickly move north choose to take along their ill-gotten fortunes, many in professional sectors have also begun emigrating en masse with the departure of their regular clientele.
strings.SKN_Under_Microscope_desc:
Like a dwelling for ants, Saint Kitts and Nevis is a microstate in every sense of the term. With a permanent population hovering just under forty-thousand and having close to no major industries, any outside influences can easily bring about disproportionate consequences to the islands' development, whether good or ill.

Due to its desperately minuscule economy, the recent lack of funds dedicated to its upkeep and ever-dwindling Canadian assistance had impacted Saint Kitts' locals' quality-of-life particularly severely in comparison to other Leeward statelets. Furthermore, the sustainability of the islands' sovereignty had also proven to be a controversial matter, with its complete reliance on foreign support bringing into question the line between a colony and a state.
strings.SKN_Malliouhana_Prey_desc:
Anguilla, the rebellious island, once named Malliouhana by its original Arawak inhabitants after a legendary sea serpent, has torn St. Kitts and Nevis asunder. The island has split off and taken with it a not insignificant part of the population and a hefty chunk of the nation's pride.

These are wounds that have yet to fully heal. Malliouhana's gambit has legitimized the concept of secession in the political discourse, especially as the Bradshaw government has doubled down on centralist policies. Nevisian separatists gather in the shadows, waiting for their moment to follow in the serpent's wake
strings.SKN_Little_Davids_Throw_desc:
The Bradshaw government has embarked on an ambitious plan of economic development for such a small island. Aiming to use his limited state resources to bolster the flailing sugar industry and its labor unions while utilizing the profits to form a meager welfare state.

But as David takes his aim, a Goliath rears his ugly head. Political dissent from moderates and the sheer strain on the budget threaten to tear the nation in two, but perhaps with enough gumption, Little David's stone will hit its mark.
strings.SKN_Sugar_Mass_desc:
Making up for the almost nonexistent domestic Saint Kitts market, some few brilliant economists had come up with the idea of an invented festival by the name of 'Sugar Mas' to garner North American tourists to this quaint statelet far down south. By blending down a slurry of vaguely Caribbean customs, Sugar Mas is a carnival celebration aiming to bring a vibrant, rejuvenated air to the otherwise unremarkable attractions of Saint Kitts.

Thanks to a willingness from both American and Canadian capital to become involved in this relatively low-stake economic project, it had proven quite popular with outside, unsuspecting tourists, though some locals still deem this artificial creation to be a little more than self-degradation.
strings.SKN_Malliouhana_Slumbers_desc:
Anguilla, the rebellious island once named Malliouhana by her original Arawak inhabitants after a legendary sea serpent, has been tamed for the time being, its secession crushed. The PAM government has made great efforts to conserve her autonomy and create a genuinely federalist form of government.

But Malliouhana's shadow still lurks just below the water, and many fear the day she will return from the depths to strike
strings.SKN_Federalist_Bulwark_desc:
Formed in part in opposition to Trinidad's ideal of a left-leaning nationalist East Caribbean Union and the more disparate cooperation of Barbados's CARICOM, the Leeward Federation seeks out a middle path. One that unites the islands around shared conservative values and a spirit of brotherly patriotism.

This opposition to the liberalizing and nationalizing trends stands out as both a new potential path for the region and a return to tradition. An emulation of the British model for a new era.
strings.SKN_Pepperpot_Stew_desc:
Like the British Leeward Islands colony before it, the Leeward Federation is a loose collection of small islands with their own unique cultures, politics, and economies. However, unlike the previous administration's incoherent pseudo-federalism, this new union strives to make the best of the situation. To bring together something greater than the sum of its parts.

Lacking a strong basis of central administration and with tensions already bubbling, it remains to be seen if this Pepperpot stew will simmer to completion or boil over.
